articles.headline: Rev. Wm. Offer
articles.summary: The Rev. William Offer preached on last Sabbath evening at Little Wesley Church, and they gave him $6.20 to aid him on his mission to California. He left this city on last Wednesday for New York, intending to take the steamer from thence.
people: preached at Little Wesley Church; missionary to California (Rev.)

articles.headline: Leaving
articles.summary: Many of our citizens are leaving the city for the watering-places. Rev. Stephen Smith and wife have gone down.
people: gone to the watering-places with his wife (Rev.)

articles.headline: Rev. H. H. Garnet's Memorial Discourse
articles.summary: We have just received a handsome copy of Rev. H. H. Garnet's Memorial Discourse. The book is gotten up in most elegant style, and comprises some 91 pages. The book may be had at our office, 619 Pine street, at One Dollar per copy.

articles.headline: Presents to Ministers
articles.author: W. H. L.
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: By perusing the Recorder of the 10th inst., I read that the Rev. James Frisby was presented with a gold-headed cane, valued at fifty-seven dollars. There is something in it to be praised, and something to be regretted. I have had the pleasure of twenty years' acquaintance with the Rev. James Frisby. (Dated Philada., June 12th, 1865; the writer would rather the class had given books. An editor's note follows.)
people: class leader presented with a gold-headed cane by a portion of his class (Rev.)

articles.headline: Harvest Home (Kaighnsville and Centreville A.M.E. Mission Sabbath Schools)
articles.summary: The A. M. E. Mission Sabbath School at Kaighnsville, New Jersey, together with the A. M. E. Mission Sabbath School at Centreville, intend having a Harvest Home on the Fourth of July, 1865, at Mr. John Star's Grove, corner of Broadway and Kaighn's Point Avenue.

articles.headline: Notice (Burlington Quarterly Meeting)
articles.author: T. Gould
articles.summary: Those of our friends, and others, from Philadelphia and vicinity, who may wish to visit Burlington, for the purpose of attending Quarterly Meeting, on the third Sabbath in July, can be accommodated with a plain dinner, at a reasonable rate, next door to the Church. Those who desire tea or coffee can also be accommodated. The proceeds are for the benefit of the Church, the members having purchased the property adjoining.

articles.headline: Notice (Chester Circuit quarterly meetings)
articles.author: Peter Gardiner
articles.summary: The Quarterly Conference for Chester Circuit will meet at Chester on Saturday evening, July 8th, at 8 o'clock. Quarterly meeting at Horntown will commence on Saturday evening, July 15th, and at Chichester July 29th, to which places the well-wishers of the Church are invited. Peter Gardiner, Preacher in charge of Chester Circuit.

articles.headline: Married (Simpson-Mann)
articles.summary: SIMPSON-MANN. On the 21st inst., by the Rev. Theo. Doughty Miller, Mr. Thomas Simpson, of this city, to Miss Margaret Mann, of Norristown. (Anglo-African, New York, please copy.)

articles.headline: Obituary (Barbara Sayres)
articles.author: S. S. D.
articles.summary: Died. Barbara, the youngest daughter of Mary and the late Benjamin Sayres, departed this life on the 5th of June, 1865, aged 13 [VERIFY age] years, 10 months, and 9 days. She was an intelligent child and beloved by all. (Verses follow, signed S. S. D. No place is stated.)
people: deceased, died June 5, 1865 (printed as Barbara, daughter of Mary and the late Benjamin Sayres)

articles.headline: Letter from Salem, N. J.
articles.author: N. H. Turpin
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: I promised to keep you posted in reference to the interesting occurrences of this city. It is a very pleasant place, situated near Fort Delaware, on the Delaware Bay. The colored people in this locality are very industrious; a large number of them are in possession of very comfortable homes. We have one day school, numbering sixty scholars; the teacher is Miss Sheppard. On the 18th, as a number of ladies and gentlemen were returning home from church, they were accosted by a number of rowdies, viz: Irishmen, which resulted in the emptying of the contents of a revolver in the body of one of those [rowdies]. (Dated Salem, N. J., June 30th, 1865; threats to mob the colored people and burn the churches on the night of the 24th followed, and extra police were put on; first quarterly meeting on the 25th; sudden death of Mr. William Hill.)
people: of Salem, N.J.; died suddenly after a fall from a second-story window (as reported)

articles.headline: The 24th U. S. C. T.
articles.summary: We have before us a letter from a non-commissioned officer of the 24th regiment, U. S. C. T., stationed at Point Lookout, Maryland, and present some items therefrom, for the benefit of those who may have friends in the regiment. This fine body of men has been doing guard duty over some 20,000 rebel prisoners at the above named point, where it is likely they will remain until all the prisoners are released. At the request of Mr. John W. Page, we have sent them fifty copies [of the Recorder].
people: 24th U.S.C.T.; at his request fifty copies of the Recorder were sent to the regiment

articles.headline: Florida Correspondence (Third Regt. U.S.C. Troops)
articles.author: Wm. B. Johnson
articles.summary: Headquarters, Post of Jacksonville, June 22, 1865. Mr. Editor: As some considerable time has elapsed since I last wrote to you and other dear friends at home, and thinking that you would like by this time to hear something further from the Third Regt. U. S. C. Troops, I accordingly seat myself to pen you a few lines. Our regiment was ordered to Tallahassee on the 19th of May. (Signed Wm. B. Johnson, Co. A, 3d U.S.C.T.; he sends thanks to the ladies of the Sanitary Commission.)

articles.headline: G. G. A. O. To All Whom This May Concern (General Grand Tabernacle, Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity)
articles.author: William H. Thomas

Wesley Church of Philadelphia, June 8th, 1865, the following Worthy Brothers and Sisters were unanimously elected to their respective positions herein named.

articles.headline: Notice (A. M. E. Zion Mission church, 7th street: appeal for aid)
articles.author: Thomas Jones
articles.summary: Philadelphia, Pa., June 27th, 1865. Know all men by these presents that we the undersigned, official members of the A. M. E. Zion Mission church, on 7th street, between Dickerson and Hecker [VERIFY] streets, have appointed and commissioned Rev. H. J. Rhodes, our Presiding Elder in charge, to collect money for the purpose of raising funds to aid us in this the hour of our great and pressing embarrassment. Our present liabilities are over twenty-two hundred dollars. Our membership is less than fifty.
people: Presiding Elder in charge, commissioned to collect money (Rev.)

articles.headline: Notice (West Philadelphia Circuit quarterly meetings)
articles.author: Jos. A. Nelson
articles.summary: Quarterly Meetings and Conference of West Philadelphia Circuit will take place as follows: Conference, July 22, at West Philadelphia, at 2 P. M. Preparatory Lecture, at Germantown, on the 28th inst., and Meeting on the 30th. Norristown, August 4th and 6th.

articles.headline: Aid for Savannah, Ga.
articles.summary: A festival was held by a committee of ladies from the Soldiers' Aid Society of Bethel A. M. E. Church, on June 3d, for the purpose of aiding the church in Savannah. Proceeds of entertainment $23.00; donation from Hornton [VERIFY] church, $4.00; individual donations, $6.00.

articles.headline: Notice (New Jersey convention to organize a State Equal Rights League)
articles.author: Samuel G. Gould
articles.summary: A convention of colored men of the State of New Jersey will meet at Trenton on the 13th of July, for the purpose of organizing a State Equal Rights League, and transacting any other business necessary to having the State represented in the National Equal Rights League, which meets in Philadelphia next September. By order, &c. Samuel G. Gould, Secretary of Trenton E. R. L.

articles.headline: Notice (District Grand Lodge No. 2, I. O. of G. S. and D. of S.: special meeting)
articles.author: W. A. K. Smith

S. and D. of S., are hereby notified to attend a special meeting of the Grand Lodge, on Monday evening, at 8 o'clock, at Masonic Hall, Eleventh street, as business of importance will be brought before the Lodge. By order of the R. W. D. C. Attest, W. A. K. Smith, R. W. G. R. S.

articles.headline: Notice (Union A. M. E. Church, Coates street: Quarterly Meeting)
articles.author: R. P. Gibbs
articles.summary: The Quarterly Meeting of the A. M. E. Union Church, Coates street, Philadelphia, will be held July 16th, 1865. R. P. Gibbs, Elder in charge.

articles.headline: A Rare Opportunity
articles.summary: A rare opportunity is now afforded to parents who desire to obtain for their children a good trade. We have been applied to by a gentleman of worth, residing in the country, to secure for him an apprentice or two to the boot-making business; would prefer to receive applications for boys of 14 or 15 years.

articles.headline: Special Notice (charges for marriage and quarterly meeting notices)
articles.summary: Brethren and friends sending us marriage notices for publication, will please remit twenty-five cents with the order, and fifty cents for each notice of quarterly meetings. The constantly increasing demand for space in our columns renders it necessary that we make this rule imperative hereafter.

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: In Philadelphia, July 2, at Mrs. H. M. Cropper's Olive Branch Boarding House, by Rev. J. P. Hamer, Mr. John Mosely [VERIFY] to Miss Caroline Parker, both of Milton, Del. On Wednesday, the 5th inst., at the residence of Mrs. Brinkley, Essex street, Philadelphia, by Rev. J. P. Hamer, Major Zaton [VERIFY] to Mary Ann Carlisle, both of Milford, Del.
people: Olive Branch Boarding House, where the first marriage took place (Mrs.)

articles.headline: In Memoriam (Charlotte Bass)
articles.author: J. H. K.
articles.summary: Vincennes, Ind., June 26th, 1865. Charlotte, wife of Rev. L. W. Bass, of the African M. E. Church, Vincennes, Indiana, died in the parsonage of said Church, June 26th, in the 54th year of her age. The deceased was born near Baltimore, and in early life was taken to the city of Philadelphia, where she remained until she reached her womanhood. Here, when quite young, she united with the African M. E. Church, and embraced religion.
people: deceased, died June 26, 1865 at Vincennes, Ind., in her 54th year; raised in Philadelphia, where she joined the African M. E. Church (printed 'Charlotte, wife of Rev. L. W. Bass')

articles.headline: The Late Dr. J. H. Wilson
articles.author: B.
articles.summary: Dr. James Henry Wilson died at 5 1/2 o'clock on Sunday Morning, 9th inst., of acute dysentery, after a short but painful illness of two weeks, in the 47th year of his age. Dr. Wilson was the eldest son of James Wilson, whose manly form and stern virtues our oldest citizens well recollect. He was carefully reared and educated under the direction of strong-minded, pious parents; went through the schools then accessible to young colored men in our city, and is remembered by those who knew him in his school-days, as a bright lad, generally at the head of his class.
people: deceased physician, died July 9, 1865 in his 47th year (Dr.; headline 'Dr. J. H. Wilson'); physician to the Home for Aged Colored Women; vestryman of St. Thomas'; of the drug store of Wilson and Peck, Lombard Street below Seventh
father of the deceased; remembered with his wife as a leading member of Bethel A.M.E. Church

articles.headline: Notice (Rev. W. D. W. Schureman at Bethel)
articles.summary: Rev. W. D. W. Schureman will (D. V.) preach at Bethel church on Sabbath afternoon, 16th inst., at 3 o'clock, at which time a collection will be taken up in aid of his church, now in course of erection at Baltimore.
people: to preach at Bethel church, July 16 (Rev.)

articles.headline: Indisposed
articles.summary: The Editor of this paper was so indisposed that he was unable to read the proof-sheets of last week's paper, which accounts for the blunder in our reply to Dr. Thompson, of the 'Advocate and Journal.' We were made to say that in our opinion there was no need for the existence of our Church as an independent body, while we wrote just the reverse. We are still unable to attend to editorial duties, but thought to be improving.

articles.headline: Dr. H. S. Phillips
articles.summary: We refer our readers to the advertisement of the above-named physician, which will be found among our notices. He claims to treat disease by a method not usually practised, and which may be very remedial. He can be consulted at 823 Race Street. His terms to those in needy circumstances are very low, and, in some cases, gratuitous.
people: practical magnetic physician, 823 Race Street (Dr.; not known to be Black)

articles.headline: The Demise of Dr. J. H. Wilson
articles.author: Sea Side
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: The loss of useful and talented men is at all times a great public calamity, but in the lamented death of such a man as Dr. Wilson, the stroke falls on us with crushing weight and tenfold severity. Dr. Wilson was well skilled in his noble department of science, and eminently successful in practice in the city of Philadelphia. (The writer adds that 'we have none other in the regular medical practice'.)

articles.headline: Notice to the Afflicted (Dr. H. S. Phillips; Madam Julien)
articles.summary: Dr. H. S. Phillips, Practical Magnetic Physician for Chronic Diseases, has taken rooms at No. 823 Race Street, Philadelphia. By this treatment, chronic diseases are cured in a few minutes. The services of Madam Julien, a remarkable (and only public colored) Clairvoyant and Trance Medium, have been secured, who will give diagnosis and prescriptions for diseases in the abnormal condition. Madam Julien is the grand-daughter of Knickerbocker, a Chief of a tribe of Kanaka Indians, and niece of Lewis Hamilton, the great Portuguese warrior. She was born on the Isle of St. Kitts. (Marked July 15-4t.)
people: practical magnetic physician, No. 823 Race Street (Dr.; not known to be Black)

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: In Philadelphia, May 18th, at the house of Mr. James Frisby, by Rev. Joshua Woodlyn, Mr. Joseph Clark, to Miss Mary Manly, of Woodbury, N. J. On June 27th, 1865, by the Rev. A. McIntosh, Mr. Jordan Burns, Miss Anna Crosy, both of Chicago. On June 28th, by the same, Mr. Henry Russell, to Miss Mary Johnson, formerly of Louisville, Ky. At Adamboro [VERIFY], Pa., on the 18th of May, by Rev. T. A. Cuff, John M. Taylor, to Sarah Elizabeth Smith, both of Newtown, Pa.
people: the marriage took place at his house in Philadelphia

articles.headline: Obituary (Julia A. Winder)
articles.author: J. Woodlyn
articles.summary: Died, on the 4th of July, 1865, near Bridgeton, N. J., Julia A. Winder, wife of Philip Winder, in the 30th year of her age. She was a very zealous and active member of the A. M. E. Church, at Greenwich, N. J., for over fourteen years, and improved every opportunity to the utmost extent of her abilities.
people: deceased, died July 4, 1865 near Bridgeton, N.J., in her 30th year; member of the A.M.E. Church at Greenwich, N.J.

articles.headline: Obituary. Dr. James H. Wilson (resolutions of the Ladies' Union Association)
articles.author: Amelia E. Mills
articles.summary: At a meeting of the Ladies' Union Association, held Monday evening, 10th inst., the following resolutions were adopted. Whereas, The Almighty has seen fit, in His unsearchable wisdom, to call from our midst by death Dr. James H. Wilson; therefore, Resolved, That we as an association have cause to mourn deeply his loss, as one of our most faithful friends, who, in the midst of opposition, did all in his power to advance the interests of the Association, and who was instrumental in gaining for us aid and friends, where otherwise all might have been a failure.
people: deceased; friend of the Ladies' Union Association (Dr.)

articles.headline: The Colored People's National Monument to the Memory of Abraham Lincoln (advertisement)
articles.author: H. H. Garnet
articles.summary: The National Lincoln Monument Association, organized in Washington, D. C., April 25, 1865, for the sole purpose of erecting a Colored People's National Monument to the memory of Abraham Lincoln. Officers: Rev. H. H. Garnet, President; James Wormley, Vice President; Stephen Smith, Philadelphia, Pa., Treasurer; Walker Lewis, Washington, D. C., Ass't Treas.; Lewis A. Bell, Recording Secretary; Wm. J. Wilson, Corresponding Secretary. (An appeal follows; the monument is to be a seat of learning, the 'National Lincoln Monumental Institute'. Marked jy 15-6m.)
people: Treasurer, National Lincoln Monument Association; Lombard Street, between Ninth and Tenth streets, Philadelphia (Rev.)
State Vice President for Pennsylvania, Philadelphia

articles.headline: The Right of Suffrage. Important Meeting.
articles.summary: A public meeting, under the auspices of the Social, Civil, and Statistical Association of the Colored people of Pennsylvania, was held in Sansom Street Hall, on Monday evening, 17th inst. The meeting was organized by the appointment of the following officers: President, I. C. Weare. (A list of Vice Presidents and Secretaries follows.) The President, Mr. Isaiah C. Weare, stated that the object of the meeting was to take measures for advocating the right of the colored people of this State, and of the whole country, to the elective franchise.
people: President of the meeting (also printed I. C. Weare)
Secretary; spoke and offered a resolution of co-operation with the Harrisburg Convention
announced as first speaker, declined from indisposition (Rev.)

articles.headline: The Philadelphia "Press" a Weather-cock
articles.summary: During the latter part of President Lincoln's term, the Press of this city steadily pursued a course which gained for it the good will of the colored citizens of Philadelphia. Since the assassination of our noble President, a most wondrous transformation has been wrought. In its leading editorial of Tuesday, the 18th instant, headed 'The Effect of Negro Suffrage on the South,' it distinctly avows itself to be no friend to the colored people.

articles.headline: Rev. John W. Stevenson
articles.summary: This able minister delivered a lecture on last Tuesday evening, in the Union Baptist church on 'Man, considered mentally, morally and physically.' The subject was handled in a manner at once worthy and becoming. On Thursday evening, 20th inst., Rev. S. delivered his able lecture on 'Courtship and Marriage,' which was by many pronounced a most thoughtful discourse. Brother Stevenson is a young man, laboring to obtain an education.
people: lecturer at the Union Baptist church (Rev.)

articles.headline: An Acknowledgment (8th U.S.C.T. collection for Wilberforce University)
articles.author: Wm. P. Woodlin
articles.summary: Near Petersburg, Va., April 28, 1865. Rev. James A. Shorter. Dear Sir: The appeal of the Trustees of the Wilberforce University for aid, in the columns of the Recorder, suggested the idea to a friend of our race, of the following collection; and I, as the agent, am happy to state, that the men of the regiment, representing at least ten different States, have responded to my solicitations with alacrity, and I am enabled to present you, as the result of my labors, the sum of $211. (Signed Wm. P. Woodlin, Musician 8th U.S.C.T., 2d brig., 2d div., 25th Army Corps. A list of about fifty subscribers of the 8th U.S.C.T., dated Chapin's Farm, Va., March 24, 1865, follows; the money was collected on the march after General Lee from Petersburg to Appomattox Court-house.)

articles.headline: An Acknowledgment (Ladies' Union Association of Philadelphia at L'Ouverture Hospital)
articles.author: C. Leonard
articles.summary: Headqrs. L'Ouverture U. S. Gen. Hosp., Alexandria, Va., July 12, 1865. Mr. Editor: Permit me, through the columns of your valuable paper, to acknowledge the receipt of a valuable donation of delicacies from the Ladies' Union Association of Philadelphia, Pa., consisting of every variety of delicacies suited to the taste of those for whom they were designed. The best of all is, that their President, Miss Amelia Mills, and Mrs. Antar [VERIFY], Mrs. Hunt, Miss Williams, and Miss Bruce [VERIFY], her assistants in her noble work, were here present in person, and distributed their donations.
people: President, Ladies' Union Association of Philadelphia (Miss)

articles.headline: Excursion (African M. E. Wesley Sabbath School)
articles.author: John A. Hughes
articles.summary: The African M. E. Wesley Sabbath School held its twenty-sixth annual excursion to Diamond Cottage, Camden, N. J., on Tuesday, June 27th. Several addresses were delivered by distinguished divines. John A. Hughes, Sup't. John Mitchell [VERIFY], Minister.

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Edith Chappel)
articles.summary: Edith Chappel left Columbia, South Carolina, on February 20th, 1865, with the army of Gen. Sherman, from the residence of Mrs. Henry Lyons. Her aunt, Fannie Bostick, can be found with Mr. A. L. Hart [VERIFY initials], 427 [VERIFY] Lombard St., Philadelphia. (Marked July 22-2t.)
people: aunt seeking Edith Chappel; to be found with Mr. A. L. Hart, Lombard St., Philadelphia
sought; left Columbia, S.C., February 20, 1865 with Sherman's army

articles.headline: Notice (Annual Meeting of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League)
articles.author: J. C. White, Jr.
articles.summary: The Annual Meeting of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League will be held at Harrisburg, Pa., on Wednesday morning, August 9th, at 10 o'clock. Societies not represented in this League are urged to make immediate arrangements for identifying themselves with it, and sending their representatives, in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution. By order of the Board, J. C. White, Jr., Sec'y. Philadelphia, July 18, 1865.

articles.headline: Minutes of P. S. E. R. League
articles.author: Jacob C. White, Jr.
articles.summary: To members of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League, and others interested in the Elective Franchise movement: The Minutes of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights Convention have been ready for some months. Members of the Convention are called upon to redeem their pledges. Minutes, $20.00 per hundred, or 25 cents per single copy. Constitutions, $5.00 per hundred, or 5 cents per single copy. Send your orders to Jacob C. White, Jr., Sec., 717 Lombard Street, Philadelphia, Pa.

articles.headline: Married (Thomas-Stevens)
articles.summary: On May 23d, 1865, in Baltimore, Md., by Rev. J. N. Mars, Mr. John Henry Thomas, of Camden, N. J., to Miss Georgianna Stevens, of Baltimore.

articles.headline: Tribute of Respect (Dr. James H. Wilson; Executive Board, Pennsylvania State Equal Rights' League)
articles.author: Jas. M'C. Crummill
articles.summary: At a meeting of the Executive Board of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights' League, held July 11th, 1865, the following resolutions, offered by Mr. Jos. C. Bustill, were unanimously adopted: Whereas, It has pleased Almighty God, in His inscrutable wisdom, to remove from labor to reward, in the prime of life, and from the sphere of usefulness, our late fellow-member, Dr. James H. Wilson, Treasurer of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights' League; therefore, be it Resolved, That in the death of Dr. James H. Wilson, Philadelphia has lost one of its brightest ornaments.
people: deceased; Treasurer of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights' League (Dr.)

articles.headline: Died (Robert Evans)
articles.summary: Died. On the 5th of July, Robert Evans, in the 70th year of his age, after a short but severe illness, which he bore with Christian resignation. His remains were conveyed to Bordentown, N. J., for interment.
people: deceased, died July 5, 1865 in his 70th year; interred at Bordentown, N.J.

articles.headline: Cape Island Correspondence
articles.author: Seaside
articles.summary: Cape Island, July 15th, 1865. (A letter on the season at Cape Island, N.J.: improvements on the island, colored women there in business for themselves, the insolence of some white Philadelphia visitors, and the remark that guests for the Banneker House come slowly.)

events.location: Mr. John Star's Grove, corner of Broadway and Kaighn's Point Avenue (Camden, N.J.)

events.name: General Grand Tabernacle of Accepted Order of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity: first Biennial Session and election

Thomas, of Washington, D.C.; General Grand Deputy Worthy Superior, N. B. Smallwood, of Providence, R.I.; General Grand Worthy Vice Superior, Sister Sarah C. events.description: Quarterly Meetings and Conference of West Philadelphia Circuit: Conference July 22 at West Philadelphia at 2 P.M.; Preparatory Lecture at Germantown on the 28th inst. and Meeting on the 30th; Norristown, August 4th and 6th. Signed Jos. A. Nelson, Preacher in charge for 1865. Notice marked July 8-3t.

events.name: Convention of colored men of New Jersey to organize a State Equal Rights League
events.description: Call for a convention of colored men of the State of New Jersey at Trenton on the 13th of July to organize a State Equal Rights League and to have the State represented in the National Equal Rights League, 'which meets in Philadelphia next September'. By order, Samuel G. Gould, Secretary of Trenton E. R. L.
attendees: Secretary of Trenton E. R. L.

events.name: Marriages by Rev. J. P. Hamer in Philadelphia (Delaware couples)
events.location: Mrs. H. M. Cropper's Olive Branch Boarding House, Philadelphia; and the residence of Mrs. Brinkley, Essex street, Philadelphia
events.description: July 2: Mr. John Mosely [VERIFY] to Miss Caroline Parker, both of Milton, Del., at Mrs. H. M. Cropper's Olive Branch Boarding House, by Rev. J. P. Hamer. Wednesday July 5: Major Zaton [VERIFY] to Mary Ann Carlisle, both of Milford, Del., at the residence of Mrs. Brinkley, Essex street, Philadelphia, by Rev. J. P. Hamer. The couples are Delaware residents and are not linked.

events.name: Death of Dr. James Henry Wilson, physician
events.description: Dr. James Henry Wilson died at 5 1/2 o'clock on Sunday morning, July 9, 1865, of acute dysentery after two weeks' illness, in the 47th year of his age. Memoir signed 'B.': eldest son of James Wilson; educated in the schools then open to young colored men in the city; barred by caste from the medical schools, he hired himself at the Academy of Natural Sciences, then in the College of Pharmacy, then at Jefferson Medical College and afterwards the Medical Department of the University of Pennsylvania, completing the curriculum of each by private study; he applied for a degree and after long equivocation the examining board answered that it was inexpedient to examine any colored candidate. Leading physicians nevertheless admitted him to consultation. Lately appointed physician to the 'Home for Aged Colored Women' (so printed). He kept a drug store in partnership with Dr. Peck, son of the Rev. John Peck of Pittsburg (Wilson and Peck, Lombard Street below Seventh), then entered practice. His parents are remembered as leading members of Bethel A.M.E. Church; he was for many years a member of St. Thomas' (Episcopal) church and often an active vestryman. 'A man of unmixed African blood, short in stature'; 'probably more widely known and beloved by the colored people of Philadelphia than any man now living'. Twice married; leaves a wife, a daughter and two sons (the youngest two years old) and one brother, the last of a family of seven. On page 3 a letter signed 'Sea Side' laments that 'we have none other in the regular medical practice', and the Ladies' Union Association prints resolutions.

events.name: Ladies' Union Association: meeting and resolutions on the death of Dr. James H. Wilson
events.description: At a meeting of the Ladies' Union Association held Monday evening, July 10, 1865, resolutions were adopted on the death of Dr. James H. Wilson: the association mourns 'one of our most faithful friends, who, in the midst of opposition, did all in his power to advance the interests of the Association, and who was instrumental in gaining for us aid and friends, where otherwise all might have been a failure'; 'we as a people have lost in him a bright evidence of our intellectual ability'; condolence to the family; the resolutions to be presented to the family and published in the Christian Recorder. Signed Amelia E. Mills, President; S. Lizzie Brown, Secretary.

events.name: Bethel Church: Rev. W. D. W. Schureman preaches; collection for his church at Baltimore
events.description: Rev. W. D. W. Schureman to preach at Bethel church on Sabbath afternoon, the 16th inst., at 3 o'clock; a collection to be taken up in aid of his church, now in course of erection at Baltimore.

events.name: Marriage of Joseph Clark and Mary Manly
events.location: The house of Mr. James Frisby, Philadelphia
events.description: In Philadelphia, May 18th, at the house of Mr. James Frisby, by Rev. Joshua Woodlyn, Mr. Joseph Clark to Miss Mary Manly, of Woodbury, N. J.

events.name: Social, Civil, and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania: public meeting on the right of suffrage
events.description: Public meeting under the auspices of the Social, Civil, and Statistical Association of the Colored people of Pennsylvania, Monday evening, July 17, 1865. Officers appointed: President, I. C. Weare (Mr. Isaiah C. Weare). Vice Presidents: U. B. Vidal, Stephen Smith, Clayton Miller, James P. Clay, Wm. Whipper, Morris Brown [VERIFY], Henry Jones, Robert Adger, Jos. M. Bustill [VERIFY], T. H. Davis, Rev. Wm. Moore, C. Simpson, Rev. E. Weaver, H. Morton, Daniel George, Wm. H. Riley, Henry Gordon, J. W. Price, S. H. Herrott [VERIFY], J. Hankinson, Wm. S. Burton [VERIFY], J. E. Glasgow, J. M. Autor [VERIFY], Joshua Brown, C. H. Bustill, B. G. Hill [VERIFY], R. Jones, S. Purnell, M. R. Robinson. Secretaries: Wm. Still, S. Morgan Smith, Raymond J. Barr [VERIFY], P. T. Smith, C. J. Houston [VERIFY], R. M. Adger, A. S. Casey [VERIFY], J. C. White, Jr., St. George Taylor, H. Johnson, R. Faucet, Thomas H. Boling. The President said the object was to take measures for advocating the right of the colored people of this State and of the whole country to the elective franchise; friends say 'You are right, but do not hold any meetings; it will all come right'; the present action of the Government tended to hand the colored man over to those who oppressed him before the war. Rev. W. J. Alston was announced as first speaker but declined from indisposition. Rev. C. W. Denison spoke (he came 'to hear colored men speak in behalf of their own rights, after speaking so well with the bayonet'), then Rev. Dr. Wood, a native of England; Messrs. Robt. Purvis and S. Morgan Smith also spoke. The Chairman offered resolutions, which were adopted: to spare no pains in pressing the claim to suffrage; to circulate Wm. D. Kelley's speech on the 'Safeguards of Personal Liberty', Fred. Douglass' address on 'Equality before the Law' and R. Dale Owen's letter to President Johnson; that the colored citizens of Philadelphia give liberally to vindicate their rights through newspapers, pamphlets and public meetings. S. Morgan Smith offered a further resolution, adopted, extending to the Convention to be assembled at Harrisburg the Association's cordial co-operation. Announced as the first of a series of meetings; well attended, 'the audience being composed of both classes'.
attendees: Secretary; spoke and offered a resolution of co-operation with the Harrisburg Convention
announced as first speaker, declined from indisposition (Rev.)

events.name: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights' League, Executive Board: meeting and resolutions on the death of Dr. James H. Wilson, Treasurer
events.description: At a meeting of the Executive Board held July 11th, 1865, resolutions offered by Mr. Jos. C. Bustill were unanimously adopted on the death of Dr. James H. Wilson, Treasurer of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights' League: 'Philadelphia has lost one of its brightest ornaments, one of its most useful and most honored citizens, and this League one of the most earnest co-laborers in the work of securing the spread of liberal sentiments and equal rights without regard to color'; condolence to the family; the members of the Executive Board to wear the usual badge of mourning for thirty days. Signed Jas. M'C. Crummill, Pres. pro tem.; attest, J. C. White, Jr., Secretary.

events.name: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League: Annual Meeting called
events.description: Notice dated Philadelphia, July 18, 1865: the Annual Meeting of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League will be held at Harrisburg on Wednesday morning, August 9th, at 10 o'clock. Societies not represented in the League are urged to identify themselves with it and send representatives in accordance with the Constitution. By order of the Board, J. C. White, Jr., Sec'y. A display advertisement of the meeting and a notice offering the Minutes and Constitutions (Jacob C. White, Jr., Sec., 717 Lombard Street) run in the same column, all marked July 22-3t.
attendees: Secretary (also printed Jacob C. White, Jr., 717 Lombard Street)

events.name: African M. E. Wesley Sabbath School: twenty-sixth annual excursion
events.description: The African M. E. Wesley Sabbath School held its twenty-sixth annual excursion to Diamond Cottage, Camden, N. J., on Tuesday, June 27th. Several addresses were delivered by distinguished divines. Signed John A. Hughes, Sup't; John Mitchell [VERIFY], Minister.

events.name: Ladies' Union Association of Philadelphia: donation and visit to L'Ouverture Hospital, Alexandria, Va.
events.location: L'Ouverture U. S. General Hospital, Alexandria, Virginia
events.description: Chaplain C. Leonard, U. S. Army, acknowledges under date July 12, 1865 a donation of delicacies from the Ladies' Union Association of Philadelphia, amounting to three hundred dollars (tea, coffee, fans, condensed milk, jellies, pickles, cakes, oranges, lemons, tamarinds, wine, honey, farina, corn starch, dried fruits, a barrel of crushed sugar, canned oysters, butter, crackers, tobacco, castile soap) and $40 in cash. The President, Miss Amelia Mills, with Mrs. Antar [VERIFY], Mrs. Hunt, Miss Williams and Miss Bruce [VERIFY], her assistants, were present in person and distributed the donations. The date of the visit is not stated; July 12 is the date of the letter.

events.name: Union Baptist church: lectures by Rev. John W. Stevenson
events.description: Rev. John W. Stevenson lectured 'on last Tuesday evening' (July 18) in the Union Baptist church on 'Man, considered mentally, morally and physically', and on Thursday evening, 20th inst., on 'Courtship and Marriage'. He is described as a young man laboring to obtain an education.
